subject: William Hartnell
hook: WILLIAM HARTNELL IS NOT WHO YOU THINK
angle: William Hartnell, best known for playing the grandfatherly Doctor in Doctor Who, spent much of his early career gaining fame for playing tough-guy military sergeants.
angle_support: He became known for tough military roles, including in the television sitcom The Army Game (1957–1961) and the film Carry On Sergeant (1958).
Hartnell's breakthrough role as a sergeant in The Way Ahead (1944), which prompted leading roles like Murder in Reverse (1945) and Appointment with Crime (1946).
title: The Forgotten Military Past of William Hartnell
description: While best remembered as the original Doctor, William Hartnell's early acting career was dominated by gritty military roles. He spent years mastering the persona of the sergeant before transitioning to his most famous character.
narration: WILLIAM HARTNELL IS NOT WHO YOU THINK You picture a grandfatherly figure in a police box. It was closer to reality that he built a massive career playing aggressive, sharp-tongued military sergeants on screen. Before his iconic sci-fi role, he anchored the television sitcom The Army Game. He later solidified this tough-guy archetype by starring in the 1958 hit film Carry On Sergeant, defining his reputation for years before the TARDIS arrived. The Doctor was once a man defined by the barracks.
